newsitem.title: USA: Chicago schools propose $3 bln budget for FY 97-98.
newsitem.headline: Chicago schools propose $3 bln budget for FY 97-98.

text.p: Chicago school officials Wednesday unveiled a proposed $2.997 billion budget for the 1997-98 school year that includes a $34 million increase in the property tax levy.
Chicago Public Schools also anticipates issuing about $500 million of general obligation bonds for the district's ongoing Capital Improvement Plan, hopefully in autumn, spokesman John Holden said.
The spending plan calls for issuing the debt sometime during the fiscal year, but school officials would like to go to the market in the fall if details can be completed, Holden said.
The improvement plan started in 1995 calls for issuing $1.4 billion of bonds for capital programs, Holden said. About $850 million of debt has been issued so far, he noted.
Holden said officials believe the schools need as much as $3 billion worth of improvements and hope to get assistance from state and federal sources as well.
"By the end of this budget year, we expect to have completed major renovation work at the majority of our school facilities, School Reform Board President Gery Chico said in a statement.
The proposed spending plan includes a $163 million increase over the current fiscal year and retains a balanced budget over the next four years, Chief Executive Officer Paul Vallas said.
About $42 million of the increase will go to teacher salary increases already under contract.
The budget calls for expanding education programs, but to a lesser extent than anticipated because of the General Assembly's failure to adopt funding reforms during the last session, Vallas said.

The proposal adds $34 million for a new summer program for some elementary and junior high school students. It also would continue expansion of early childhood programs and provide $2 million to keep teen mothers in school and provide early childhood development for their children.
The plan is to be submitted to Chicago School Reform Board of Trustees Wednesday for adoption before the start of the academic year in late August.
